data.name: Home.Faq.Lead
data.value: Quick answers about how Academia Auditiva works.

data.name: Home.Faq1.Q
data.value: Do I need to know music theory?

data.name: Home.Faq1.A
data.value: No. Every exercise comes with instructions and tips, and you can start with single notes before moving on to intervals and chords.

data.name: Home.Faq2.Q
data.value: Does it work on my phone?

data.name: Home.Faq2.A
data.value: Yes. It runs in the browser on phones, tablets and computers, with nothing to install. Headphones help.

data.name: Home.Faq3.A
data.value: Portuguese (Brazil), English and French. You can switch at any time from the menu at the top of the page.

data.name: Home.Faq4.Q
data.value: I'm a teacher. How do I create a class?

data.name: Home.Faq4.A
data.value: Create your account and ask the administrator to enable the teacher profile. The teacher area then appears in the top menu, where you create classes, invite students by email and assign routines.

data.name: Home.Faq5.A
data.value: Nine: note recognition, intervals (by number and by full name), melodic intervals, chords, chord quality, harmonic function, comparing two melodies and sight-singing.

data.name: Home.Faq6.A
data.value: Yes. Creating an account and training cost nothing.

data.value: Create your free account and start with your first exercise.

data.name: Exercise.GuessNote.Instructions
data.value: Listen to the note that plays and pick the matching note from the available options.

data.name: Exercise.GuessNote.Tip1
data.value: Listen more than once if you need to.

data.name: Exercise.GuessNote.Tip2
data.value: Try singing the note to compare with your inner reference.

data.name: Exercise.GuessNote.Tip3
data.value: Compare it to notes you know well, such as C or A.

data.name: Exercise.GuessChords.Instructions
data.value: Listen to the chord and select the matching chord type.

data.name: Exercise.GuessChords.Tip1
data.value: Pay attention to the feeling: major sounds happy, minor sounds sad.

data.name: Exercise.GuessChords.Tip2
data.value: Compare against reference chords if you need to.

data.name: Exercise.GuessChords.Tip3
data.value: Try singing the notes to feel whether the intervals are major or minor.

data.name: Exercise.GuessInterval.Instructions
data.value: Listen to the two notes and identify the distance between them (interval).

data.name: Exercise.GuessInterval.Tip1
data.value: Associate intervals with songs you know (e.g. major third = "Happy Birthday").

data.name: Exercise.GuessInterval.Tip2
data.value: Listen again and sing the notes.

data.name: Exercise.GuessInterval.Tip3
data.value: Notice whether the sound is close (second) or wide (fifth, octave...).

data.name: Exercise.GuessQuality.Instructions
data.value: Listen to the chord and decide whether it is major, minor or diminished.

data.name: Exercise.GuessQuality.Tip1
data.value: Try to memorize the typical sound of each quality.

data.name: Exercise.GuessQuality.Tip2
data.value: Diminished chords sound tense or unstable.

data.name: Exercise.GuessQuality.Tip3
data.value: Compare with simple chords you already know.

data.name: Exercise.GuessFunction.Instructions
data.value: Listen to the chord in context and identify its function (tonic, dominant, subdominant).

data.name: Exercise.GuessFunction.Tip1
data.value: Listen to the whole progression first to anchor the key.

data.name: Exercise.GuessFunction.Tip2
data.value: The tonic feels like home; the dominant pulls back to it.

data.name: Exercise.GuessFunction.Tip3
data.value: Subdominant chords feel like a soft step away from the tonic.

data.name: Exercise.GuessFullInterval.Instructions
data.value: Listen to the interval and identify both the distance and its quality (major, minor, perfect, etc.).

data.name: Exercise.GuessFullInterval.Tip1
data.value: Identify the size first, then refine to the quality.

data.name: Exercise.GuessFullInterval.Tip2
data.value: Major and minor differ by one semitone.

data.name: Exercise.GuessMissingNote.Instructions
data.value: Listen to two melodies and tell whether they are the same or whether something changed.

data.name: Exercise.GuessMissingNote.Tip1
data.value: Pay attention to the central notes of the melody.

data.name: Exercise.GuessMissingNote.Tip2
data.value: If you are unsure, listen more than once.

data.name: Exercise.GuessMissingNote.Tip3
data.value: Singing or tapping the melody helps memorization.

data.name: Exercise.IntervalMelodico.Instructions
data.value: Listen to the melody and identify the first scale degree, the last one, and the intervals between the first two and the last two notes.

data.name: Exercise.IntervalMelodico.Tip1
data.value: Find the key of the melody first.

data.name: Exercise.IntervalMelodico.Tip2
data.value: Pay attention to the first and last notes to determine the degrees.

data.name: Exercise.IntervalMelodico.Tip3
data.value: Compare the intervals to ones you already know.

data.name: Exercise.IntervalMelodico.Tip4
data.value: Use scales as a reference for the degrees.

data.name: Exercise.SolfegeMelody.Instructions
data.value: Click “New melody” and read the melody on the staff. Listen to the starting note, click “Record” and sing the melody, then click “Validate”. Any octave is fine.

data.name: Exercise.SolfegeMelody.Tip1
data.value: Look carefully at the pitches on the staff.

data.name: Exercise.SolfegeMelody.Tip2
data.value: Sing slowly to make sure you are accurate.

data.name: Exercise.SolfegeMelody.Tip3
data.value: If needed, practice the scale before attempting.

data.name: Exercise.SolfegeMelody.Tip4
data.value: Your recording is analyzed in your browser and never leaves your device.
